body.condition: \(0\le\lambda_j^a(t)\le L\) for every \(a\in\{0,1\}\), \(j\in\{1,2\}\), and almost every \(t\in[0,T]\).

novel.justification: The common numerical ceiling is a maintained identifying and sensitivity restriction, not a standard consequence of separable-effects theory. A valid value can be prespecified from an external exact-time registry or audited event-trigger system that supplies a scientifically certified envelope \(\lambda_j^a(t)\le L_{aj}(t)\) over the protocol window: take \(L:=\sup_{a,j,t}L_{aj}(t)\) and round upward. This route is realistic for endpoints monitored by an externally validated surveillance system with a documented maximum event intensity; when only a more conservative envelope is defensible, the analysis is repeated at \(\bar L\).
